result.rationale: The diff's refreshOAuthTokens sends only calcomUserId and appSlug to the sync endpoint, and the new webhook handler itself uses findFirst on {userId, appId} ('Can't use prisma upsert as we don't know the id of the credential'), indicating the code assumes/permits ambiguity when multiple credentials exist per user/app. If a user has multiple accounts for one app, the proxy cannot address the correct credential, returning another account's token — a correctness defect in the newly introduced flow, not contradicted by anything in the diff.

judged_text: packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts:10 — `calcomUserId: userId.toString(), appSlug` identifies only a user/app pair and cannot identify which credential to refresh when one user connects multiple accounts for the same app, so the proxy can return another account's token; rebuttal requires a database-enforced one-credential-per-user/app invariant, which the create-only callback flow does not establish.

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies that refreshOAuthTokens.ts sends only userId and appSlug to the credential sync endpoint (lines 10-11). Looking at the diff, when a user has multiple credentials for the same app (e.g., multiple Google Calendar accounts), this identifier pair cannot distinguish between them. The webhook endpoint in app-credential.ts uses findFirst with userId and appId, which would return an arbitrary credential when multiple exist. The callback handlers use createOAuthAppCredential which creates new credentials without enforcing uniqueness. This is a real bug where token refresh could return/update the wrong account's tokens.
